text:
elaine-android: Noticed duplicate side-effects when uploading from emulator during mobile network handoff. Two POSTs make it to backend for one user action.

sam-sre: That usually means a retry kicked in after the connection dropped. Which OkHttp settings and what RequestBody are you using?

elaine-android: We use our wrapper RequestBody that streams from an InputStream for memory reasons. OkHttp client is mostly default, e.g.:
```
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .connectTimeout(8, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .callTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build();
```
The interceptor tries to recreate the body by calling `createStream()` on the original payload object.

nate-sdk: Streaming bodies + retryOnConnectionFailure can be a problem. OkHttp will only retry if it believes the request is idempotent or the body can be replayed. If your wrapper claims repeatable when it's not, you'll see this.

elaine-android: Repro steps I used:
1) Emulator API 31
2) Start upload via sample app (10KB JSON)
3) During upload toggle airplane mode on/off rapidly
Server log excerpt:
```
2026-03-22T16:12:01Z POST /files 200 user=elaine id=xyz
2026-03-22T16:12:02Z POST /files 200 user=elaine id=xyz
```

sam-sre: Quick experiments: try returning a RequestBody that explicitly overrides `isOneShot()`/`contentLength()` semantics or disable retryOnConnectionFailure. Also try buffering small payloads into a byte[] to make them repeatable.

nate-sdk: We should also audit our ReplayInterceptor. If it calls `request.newBuilder().method(request.method(), newBody)` without preserving the original request metadata OkHttp might decide to re-enqueue. For SDK safety, add an opt-in config: `enableSmallUploadBuffering(true)` and set a size threshold (e.g., 64KB).

elaine-android: I quickly toggled `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` and could only repro the single POST. Buffering fix looks promising for small files. For large ones we should document the behavior clearly.

nate-sdk: Agreed. I'll add a unit test in samples/ that simulates socket close during write and asserts single request when buffering enabled. Also update the Android SDK migration guide about non-idempotent uploads and duplicate side-effects.

ci-bot: Issue #2401 created: "android-sdk: duplicate-upload-on-network-handoff (streaming-body-retry)" assigned to nate-sdk

sam-sre: Add a note to changelog and recommend server-side dedupe by idempotency-key for uploads.

elaine-android: Will draft the PR with the buffering opt-in and a FAQ entry about why retries happen :slightly_smiling_face:

nate-sdk: Thanks — please include the small sample app and emulator repro steps in the issue so QA can validate on device/emulator.
